original_question: Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces admit finite manifold quotients that are Laplace-isospectral but not isometric?
target_in_paper: Question 1.15 (§1.5): "Which compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces cover isospectral and non-isometric manifolds?"
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the right ambient objects—compact simply connected irreducible symmetric spaces—and the right phenomenon: the existence of non-isometric manifold quotients that are isospectral for the Laplace-Beltrami operator. It also correctly stays in the manifold setting rather than drifting to orbifolds.
missing_details: The paper phrases the problem as whether a compact simply connected irreducible symmetric space X "covers" isospectral and non-isometric manifolds; to make the question stand-alone, one should spell out that this means there exist two compact quotient manifolds X/Γ1 and X/Γ2.
The quotients should be described as coming from finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 of Isom(X) acting freely by isometries, with the induced Riemannian metrics.
Isospectrality should be specified as equality of the Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions, counted with multiplicities; the draft leaves this implicit in the phrase "Laplace-isospectral."
The question is about the existence of a pair of quotient manifolds with the same spectrum and different isometry class, not merely about admitting some finite quotient.

The scope should remain exactly the manifold problem of Question 1.15; orbifold variants are separated later as Problem 7.7, and non-simply connected group-type variants are separated as Question 7.6.

No algebraic base field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency parameters are relevant here; the hidden assumptions are geometric: compactness, simple connectedness, irreducibility, symmetry, free finite isometric action, and the induced quotient metric.
refined_question: Let X be a compact simply connected irreducible symmetric space, equipped with its symmetric Riemannian metric. For which such X do there exist finite subgroups Γ1, Γ2 ⊂ Isom(X) acting freely by isometries such that the quotient manifolds X/Γ1 and X/Γ2, with the induced Riemannian metrics, have the same Laplace-Beltrami spectrum on functions (counted with multiplicities) but are not isometric?
justification: The draft clearly targets the compact-type analogue of McReynolds' theorem formulated in Question 1.15, not the earlier questions from §§1.1–1.4. The introduction states the official problem in that classification form, and Section 7 restates it before giving partial answers. The nearby context shows why the question must stay narrow: some compact irreducible symmetric spaces do not cover any manifold at all; Theorem 7.1 handles odd-dimensional spheres and certain real Grassmannians; Proposition 7.4 and Theorem 1.16 treat the group-type case via almost conjugate but non-conjugate finite subgroups of compact simple Lie groups; and orbifolds are explicitly postponed to Problem 7.7. So the paper-faithful stand-alone version is the official Question 1.15 with the quotient mechanism and the Laplace-spectrum meaning made explicit, but without broadening to orbifolds or to non-simply connected spaces.
